title: Garter stitch mittens
subtitle: Simple full mittens in garter stitch, worked flat and seamed.
excerpt: Full mittens in garter stitch, worked flat in DK wool and seamed up the side. Afterthought thumb. A good stepping stone between learning garter stitch on a scarf and knitting a three-dimensional object. Sized for 18, 20, and 22 cm hand circumferences.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 1st series (1880s), §Plain knitted mittens. Flat garter stitch mittens seamed up the side are among the simplest mitten constructions in the Victorian knitting canon. Both Weldon's and Beeton's Book of Needlework (1870) include versions. Both are out of UK and EU copyright.

glossaryTerms.definition: The simplest knitted fabric, produced by knitting every stitch on every row when working flat. The resulting fabric has a ridged texture on both sides and lies flat without curling.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.

content.text: Full mittens worked flat in
garter stitch
and seamed up the side, with an
afterthought thumb
, sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

Garter stitch is worked flat with every row knitted. The mitten is a single rectangle seamed into a tube, with the top shaped by decreases. The thumb uses the afterthought method: a row of waste yarn marks the thumb position during knitting, and the thumb is worked after the hand is complete. This construction needs only straight needles and one stitch technique. Budget about 90 g (200 m / 220 yards) of DK wool per pair.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 90 g (about 200 m / 220 yards) of DK-weight wool

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) straight or circular needles

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the afterthought thumb

content.text: Gauge

20 stitches and 36 rows to 10 cm in garter stitch on 4 mm needles. Garter stitch gauge differs from stocking stitch gauge: garter rows are shorter, so you need more rows per 10 cm. Measure your swatch relaxed and flat.
Stitches used
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count and measurement reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and hand body
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 36 (40, 44) stitches. Knit every row for 18 (20, 22) rows. The piece measures about 5 (5.5, 6) cm.
Thumb marker row

On a right-side row: knit 8 (9, 10) stitches with waste yarn, slip those stitches back to the left needle, then knit them again with the working yarn. Continue in garter stitch to end of row. The waste yarn marks the thumb position.
Hand above thumb
Continue in garter stitch for 24 (28, 32) more rows. The piece from cast-on measures about 12 (13, 14) cm.
Mitten top shaping

Decrease row (RS): k1, ssk, knit to last 3 stitches, k2tog, k1. Next row: knit all stitches. Repeat these 2 rows until 8 stitches remain. Cut yarn and draw through all 8 stitches. Pull tight to close.
Seaming

Fold the mitten in half with the right sides together. The seam runs along the side edge from the cast-on to the tip. Seam using mattress stitch (or overcast stitch for simplicity), leaving the seam open at the thumb-marker row: do not seam across the waste yarn. The side opening at the thumb marker is where the thumb was knitted.
Thumb
Remove the waste yarn from the thumb marker row. Pick up 8 (9, 10) stitches above and 8 (9, 10) stitches below the gap. Total: 16 (18, 20) stitches.

Work garter stitch flat on these stitches for 10 (12, 12) rows. Decrease row: k1, ssk, knit to last 3, k2tog, k1. Knit one row. Repeat until 4 stitches remain. Draw yarn through and close. Seam the thumb side.
Mirror your second mitt

Work the second mitt identically. Because the mitten is flat and seamed, the only adjustment needed is to place the waste yarn at the opposite side: on the second mitten, knit to the last 8 (9, 10) stitches before working them in waste yarn.
Common faults
Top of the mitten does not close flat: the decreases were not balanced, with more rows on one side than the other. The decrease row and the plain row must alternate evenly.
Garter ridge count is wrong on the second mitten: the first and second mittens should have the same number of ridges. Count garter ridges rather than individual rows.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. The garter fabric does not need blocking, but a damp press helps neaten the seam.
Care
Hand wash in cool water with a wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next
The in-the-round version of these mittens uses the same top shaping but works in stocking stitch and removes the seam step. That is the standard beginner mitten construction at the next stage.
